extracted.intended_audience: researchers and program evaluators studying grant-writing interventions (ASBMB/IMAGE), and stakeholders interested in workshop impact
extracted.subtask_description: Protocol/registration for a longitudinal quasi-experimental evaluation of a grant-writing workshop (IMAGE) comparing workshop participants to a matched comparison group, tracking funding outcomes and potential mediators across time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design: longitudinal quasi-experimental
rubrics_metrics.description: These are the results of a longitudinal quasi-experimental study started in 2015 to measure the impact of the ASBMB's grant-writing workshop - IMAGE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implements a quasi-experimental (non-randomized) longitudinal design initiated in 2015; implies repeated measurement over time to assess change attributable to workshop participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant groups: IMAGE workshop participants and matched comparison group
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two matched groups of participants: IMAGE workshop participants and a matched comparison group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation compares outcomes between the workshop cohort and a separately matched comparison group; matching procedures and balance diagnostics are implied though not detailed on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome metric: securing grant funding within two years
rubrics_metrics.description: We anticipate that the IMAGE workshop participants will secure grant funding in the first two years after the workshop at a higher rate than the match comparison group participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary outcome is rate/proportion of participants obtaining grant funding within two years post-workshop; implies binary/time-to-event measurement and group-level rate comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary hypothesis: higher funding rate for workshop participants
rubrics_metrics.description: We anticipate that the IMAGE workshop participants will secure grant funding in the first two years after the workshop at a higher rate than the match comparison group participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directional hypothesis comparing funding success between groups; evaluation should include statistical tests comparing rates and effect size estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediators: science identity and grant-writing self-efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: We expect that science identity and grant-writing self-efficacy will be significant mediators of this effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates planned mediation analysis to test whether changes in science identity and grant-writing self-efficacy explain the relationship between workshop participation and funding outcomes; requires measuring these constructs and appropriate mediation modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection frequency: surveyed twice per year
rubrics_metrics.description: Both groups of participants were tracked across time and surveyed twice per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome and mediator data collected semiannually; supports longitudinal analyses and temporal ordering for mediation, but requires handling of repeated measures and potential attrition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preregistration / open-science disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: OSF registration: Osf_registration_doi 10.17605/OSF.IO/EDSHK; Osf_registration_schema 'Preregistration Template from AsPredicted.org'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study protocol is preregistered on OSF using a recognized template, implying pre-specified hypotheses and analysis plans to reduce researcher degrees of freedom; useful for transparency and replication.
